items.title: Effectiveness of a Structured Nursing Intervention on Knowledge, Fatigue, Activities of Daily Living, and Self-Efficacy Among Patients With Myasthenia Gravis: A Quasi-Experimental Two-Group Study.
items.authors: Eman Ali Metwaly Badr, Amal Hemed Hamad, Samah Elawady Bassam, Mohamed Goda Elbqry, Fatma Mohamed Elmansy
items.abstract: Myasthenia gravis is a chronic autoimmune neuromuscular disorder that negatively affects patients' physical functioning, daily activities, and psychological well-being. Patients commonly experience fatigue and reduced self-efficacy, which may impair their ability to perform activities of daily living independently. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of a structured nursing intervention on patients' knowledge, fatigue, activities of daily living, and self-efficacy among patients with myasthenia gravis. A quasi-experimental two-group design was conducted in the neurological department at Zagazig University Hospitals, Egypt, following the TREND reporting guidelines. A purposive sample of 80 adults with myasthenia gravis was sequentially allocated to a control group (n = 40) followed by a study group (n = 40) to minimize contamination. Data were collected using the Patient Interviewing Questionnaire, Myasthenia Gravis Fatigue Scale, Myasthenia Gravis Activities of Daily Living Scale, and General Self-Efficacy Scale. Continuous outcome scores were analysed using linear mixed-effects models incorporating group, time, and group × time interactions, with adjustment for relevant baseline covariates. Compared with the control group, patients in the study group demonstrated greater improvements over time in knowledge and self-efficacy and greater reductions in fatigue and MG-ADL impairment. Adjusted linear mixed-effects analyses showed significant group × time interactions for knowledge (B = 11.10, 95% CI: 10.31-11.89), fatigue (B = -41.25, 95% CI: -44.86 to -37.64), MG-ADL impairment (B = -10.72, 95% CI: -12.05 to -9.39), and self-efficacy (B = 17.84, 95% CI: 15.91-19.77), all p < 0.001. The findings provide preliminary evidence that the structured nursing intervention was associated with improvements in knowledge, fatigue, MG-ADL impairment, and self-efficacy among patients with myasthenia gravis. Given the non-randomized design and baseline group differences, causal attribution remains limited. Further adequately powered randomized controlled trials or rigorously controlled prospective studies are needed to confirm these findings.

items.title: Symptom network structure and its association with quality of life in myasthenia gravis: a cross-sectional study.
items.authors: Yaoyi Huang, Yinxuan Wang, Xunnuo Cai, Hailing Bu, Yunying Yang, Yuying Yan
items.abstract: Myasthenia gravis (MG) is characterized by heterogeneous symptoms that often co-occur and may collectively impair quality of life (QOL). This study aimed to characterize symptom burden and symptom interrelationships in patients with MG and to examine the associations between symptom clusters and QOL. In this cross-sectional study, 220 patients with MG recruited from a tertiary hospital in China between March 2025 and February 2026 completed the Myasthenia Gravis Symptom Cluster Scale and the 15-item Myasthenia Gravis Quality of Life Scale. Network analysis was used to estimate symptom interrelationships, identify central and bridge symptoms, and assess node predictability. Hierarchical linear regression was performed to examine symptom clusters independently associated with QOL. The most prevalent symptoms were ptosis, upper limb weakness, diplopia, anxiety, and lower limb weakness. Dysphagia had the highest estimated strength and expected influence. Anxiety had the highest bridge strength, and the psychological symptom cluster showed the highest centrality in the symptom-cluster network. Greater generalized and psychological symptom-cluster burden was independently associated with poorer QOL. Dysphagia and anxiety may warrant priority assessment in patients with MG. The observed associations of psychological and generalized symptom clusters with QOL warrant further examination in longitudinal and intervention studies.
items.zhSummary: 本研究旨在分析重症肌无力（MG）患者的症状负担及其相互关系，并探讨症状聚类与生活质量（QOL）之间的关联。研究采用横断面设计，纳入220例中国三级医院的MG患者，应用症状聚类量表和生活质量量表进行评估，通过网络分析确定症状的中心性和桥接作用及节点可预测性，分层线性回归分析症状聚类对生活质量的独立影响。结果显示复视、上肢无力、眼睑下垂、焦虑和下肢无力为最常见症状，吞咽困难在网络中具有最高的强度和影响力，焦虑表现为最高的桥接症状，心理症状聚类在网络中中心性最高。广泛性和心理症状聚类负担较重与生活质量下降独立相关。研究提示吞咽困难和焦虑需优先评估，心理和广泛性症状对生活质量影响的机制需进一步纵向和干预研究验证。

items.title: Beyond Lipid-Lowering and Stroke Prevention: Unraveling the Role of Statins in Neurological Diseases.
items.authors: Nikolaos Nektarios Karamanolis, Natalia G Vallianou, Maria Dalamaga, Apostolos Evangelopoulos, Myrsini Ronioti, Dimitris C Kounatidis
items.abstract: Background: Statins are established therapies for reducing cardiovascular and cerebrovascular risk. Beyond their lipid-lowering effects, they exert pleiotropic actions, including anti-inflammatory, immunomodulatory, antioxidant, anti-apoptotic, and vascular effects. Methods: This narrative review explores the effects of statins in a range of characteristic neurological disorders beyond stroke prevention, encompassing migraine, neurodegenerative and neuroinflammatory diseases, myasthenia gravis (MG), traumatic brain injury (TBI), brain tumors, epilepsy, and peripheral neuropathy (PN). A literature search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, and Scopus, focusing on proposed mechanisms of action, clinical outcomes, and potential neurological adverse effects. Results: Research suggests potential benefits of statins in migraine, TBI and its complications, brain tumors, and epilepsy. Favorable findings have also been reported in neurodegenerative and neuroinflammatory conditions, including Parkinson's disease, Huntington's disease, and multiple sclerosis. Despite earlier concerns regarding a possible association between statin use and an increased risk of dementia, subsequent studies have challenged this association, with some suggesting even a protective effect. Potential neurological adverse effects also warrant attention, particularly the reported association between statin exposure and new-onset or worsening MG. In contrast, data linking statin use to amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and PN are controversial and do not support causality. Interpretation of the available findings is complicated by heterogeneity in statin type and lipophilicity, dosage, treatment duration, disease stage, and study design. Clinical evidence is derived predominantly from observational studies, which are susceptible to confounding and other methodological limitations. Randomized controlled trials remain relatively few, with some further limited by small sample sizes. Conclusions: The pleiotropic properties of statins provide a rationale for investigating their potential therapeutic role across a broad spectrum of neurological disorders. Nevertheless, the available evidence remains heterogeneous and, in several conditions, conflicting. Further adequately powered randomized controlled trials are needed to establish whether statins translate their proposed pleiotropic effects into clinically meaningful benefits in specific neurological disorders and to better characterize their potential neurological risks.

items.title: Optimizing Eculizumab and Ravulizumab Initiation in Myasthenia Gravis: Infection Risk, Vaccination Timing, and Antibiotic Prophylaxis.
items.authors: Ali A Habib, Thomas Edward Ragole, Amanda L Piquet, Rosemarie Walch, Tanvi Shekhar-Guturja, Cassandra L Uchida
items.abstract: Myasthenia gravis (MG) is an autoimmune neuromuscular disorder characterized by fatigable muscle weakness and fluctuating symptoms. Complement component 5 inhibitor therapies (C5ITs) such as ravulizumab and eculizumab are rapidly acting treatments for generalized MG (gMG) but associated with an increased risk of meningococcal infection. As such, an ideal strategy for initiating C5IT requires effective mitigation of meningococcal infection risk that permits timely amelioration of disease burden. While C5ITs are approved for several indications, this review focuses on gMG. The available data on infection risk associated with eculizumab and ravulizumab are discussed, and practical approaches for starting these medications are presented. Previously, C5IT could be started 2 weeks after the initial doses of meningococcal vaccines. The 2024 updates to meningococcal vaccination policies in the United States extended the completion schedule from 2 months to 6 months and allowed for clinical judgment in initiating C5ITs earlier. In treating patients whose severity of gMG necessitates starting C5ITs before the 6-month vaccination schedule can be completed, clinicians need to consider several factors, including the risk of meningococcal infection, whether the expected reduction in disease burden and improvement in quality of life justify the infection risk, and the potential complications of prolonged antibiotic prophylaxis as an infection risk mitigation strategy. In our opinion, data used to support the change in vaccine schedule did not show a substantial difference in seroresponses. Since C5ITs are likely to remain an important treatment option for gMG, consideration of early vaccination after the diagnosis is recommended to minimize delays in the initiation of C5ITs. Clinical trial data suggest that risk of meningococcal infection in patients with gMG is low, particularly during the first 6 months after C5IT initiation. The evidence supporting the use of extended antibiotic prophylaxis in this patient population is currently scarce. However, clinicians must ensure that the patient is fully aware of the risk, the symptoms of meningococcal disease, and the need for prompt medical attention if those symptoms occur. By taking a comprehensive, individualized approach, clinicians can facilitate the safe and effective use of C5ITs in patients with gMG.

items.abstract: Myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1) can rarely mimic myasthenia gravis, presenting with fluctuating ptosis and fatigability. This case emphasizes the importance of careful phenotypic evaluation, family history.

items.title: Advances in the management of myasthenia gravis.
items.authors: Nicolaas C Anderson, Sarah H Berth
items.abstract: Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder of the neuromuscular junction characterised by fluctuating fatigable weakness of skeletal muscles. Advances have led to the identification of distinct antibody subtypes and expanding therapeutic options, transforming myasthenia gravis from a disease of significant morbidity and mortality to one that is increasingly manageable. This review presents a comprehensive overview of myasthenia gravis, including its epidemiology, pathogenesis, classification, diagnostic strategies, and treatment modalities. Established therapies are discussed, including acetylcholinesterase inhibitors, corticosteroids, conventional oral immunosuppressants, intravenous immunoglobulin, plasma exchange, B cell depleting agents, complement inhibitors, neonatal fragment crystallisable receptor inhibitors, and thymectomy. A dedicated section highlights emerging treatments. Special considerations for pregnancy, myasthenic crisis, and individualised treatment approaches are emphasised. Physician-patient communication is highlighted as a critical factor in optimising adherence and outcomes. Effective integration of novel therapies into clinical practice depends on a clear understanding of their mechanisms, safety profiles, and applicability across diverse patient populations. As therapeutic complexity increases, improved clinical outcomes will require continued refinement of clinical tools, treatment algorithms, optimal communication strategies, and robust data to guide evidence based decision making.

items.title: Clinical Characteristics, Management Patterns, and Outcomes of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-Associated Myocarditis: A Single-Center Retrospective Descriptive Study.
items.journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
items.authors: Ying Zhang, Houyu Duan, Gaoran Xu, Junyuan Yang
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis (ICI-AM) is rare but potentially fatal. We retrospectively reviewed pre-existing clinical records of 42 patients diagnosed with ICI-AM at Renmin Hospital of Wuhan University between October 2023 and March 2025 and classified them as mild (grade 1-2, n = 29) or severe (grade 3-4, n = 13). Baseline characteristics, electrocardiographic findings, biomarkers, treatment patterns, and clinical outcomes were summarized descriptively. Follow-up information was retrospectively obtained from available clinical records, with an administrative follow-up end date of 31 January 2026. Severe ICI-AM was characterized by more frequent dyspnea, concomitant myasthenia gravis, electrocardiographic abnormalities, and higher troponin, CK-MB, and myoglobin levels, together with more frequent corticosteroid, intravenous immunoglobulin, and additional immunosuppressive treatment. Concomitant myositis was also more frequently observed in severe cases. During follow-up, 13 patients (31.0%) died, including 6 of 13 (46.2%) patients with severe ICI-AM and 7 of 29 (24.1%) with mild ICI-AM. Severe ICI-AM showed a more clinically overt phenotype, frequent neuromuscular involvement, and substantial all-cause mortality. These descriptive findings highlight the clinical heterogeneity of ICI-AM and require further investigation in larger prospective multicenter studies.

items.title: Muscular Rapsyn safeguards neuromuscular junction integrity during development and adult maintenance.
items.authors: Yao Wang, Liangjing Pan, Chunyang Hou, Tianyu Hu, Yu Zhang, Xinsheng Lai
items.abstract: Rapsyn is a pivotal scaffolding protein required for clustering nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs) at the neuromuscular junction (NMJ). Mutations in Rapsyn are a well-established cause of congenital myasthenic syndromes (CMS), leading to early-onset muscle weakness. However, although Rapsyn is expressed exclusively in skeletal muscle, the specific contribution of muscle-derived Rapsyn to NMJ development and stability has never been directly tested. Previous studies using in vivo Rapsyn silencing suggested a role for Rapsyn in adult NMJ maintenance, but the specific contribution of muscle-derived Rapsyn and the threshold level requirement to maintain adult NMJ integrity remain incompletely understood. Using muscle-specific and inducible Rapsyn knockout mouse models, we examined the role of muscle-derived Rapsyn in NMJ formation, structural maintenance, and neuromuscular function across developmental and adult stages. Homozygous muscular Rapsyn ablation caused neonatal lethality and catastrophic NMJ disorganization. In contrast, grade reduction of Rapsyn expression in adult mice progressively induced fragmented nAChR clusters and activity-dependent neuromuscular dysfunction despite relatively preserved gross NMJ morphology. These findings indicate that reduced Rapsyn expression destabilizes postsynaptic receptor domains and produces features resembling postsynaptic dysfunction observed in myasthenic disorders. This study demonstrates that sustained muscular Rapsyn expression is required for lifelong NMJ integrity and identifies a dose-dependent requirement for maintaining postsynaptic stability. Our findings complement previous studies demonstrating the protective effects of Rapsyn augmentation in experimental autoimmune MG by providing genetic evidence that sustained muscular Rapsyn expression is required for lifelong NMJ stability and postsynaptic resilience.

items.title: Design, Binding Profiles, and Therapeutic Potential of Imidazole- and Benzimidazole-Containing Cholinesterase Inhibitors: A Review.
items.authors: Asmaa Saleh, Dina H Dawood, Najla A Altwaijry, Lama A Alshabani, Aladdin M Srour
items.abstract: Cholinesterase enzymes, specifically acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and butyrylcholinesterase (BChE), play a central role in regulating cholinergic neurotransmission. In neurodegenerative conditions such as Alzheimer's disease (AD), a significant imbalance occurs: AChE activity declines by up to 67% in key brain regions like the hippocampus and temporal lobe, whereas BChE expression increases by up to 165%. Consequently, dual- or targeted inhibition of AChE and BChE remains a pivotal strategy in neuropharmacology to restore synaptic acetylcholine levels, manage cognitive decline, and alleviate symptoms in related neuromuscular conditions like myasthenia gravis. Although FDA-approved therapeutics (such as donepezil, rivastigmine, and galantamine) offer symptomatic relief, their clinical utility is frequently limited by peripheral cholinergic adverse effects and disease progression, driving the search for novel structural classes. Recently, imidazole- and benzimidazole-bearing scaffolds have gained significant traction as versatile structural modules in inhibitor design. Owing to their unique hydrogen-bonding capacity, basicity, and electronic characteristics, these heterocyclic cores participate in key noncovalent interactions within the catalytic and peripheral anionic sites of both enzymes. This review provides a comprehensive compilation of imidazole- and benzimidazole-containing cholinesterase inhibitors, detailing their structural design strategies, enzyme binding mechanisms, and key molecular docking interactions to provide a valuable framework for the rational development of next-generation anti-Alzheimer therapeutics.

items.title: Perioperative immune optimization and surgical readiness in thymoma-associated myasthenia gravis: current evidence and emerging strategies.
items.authors: Linlin Wang, Zhihan Wang, Yong Feng
items.abstract: Thymoma-associated myasthenia gravis (TAMG) complicates perioperative management because neurological vulnerability must be weighed against the physiological demands of tumor resection. This review examines operation-specific assessment and rapid immune optimization, compares established treatments with emerging neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) inhibition, and proposes a dual-axis framework integrating myasthenia gravis (MG)-related vulnerability and anticipated operative burden. Intravenous immunoglobulin and plasma exchange remain the established rapid-treatment options when clinically meaningful improvement is needed before surgery. FcRn inhibition provides a mechanistically distinct means of lowering circulating immunoglobulin G. Among FcRn inhibitors, efgartigimod has the most direct perioperative evidence in TAMG, but available studies are small, nonrandomized, and largely confined to selected adults with acetylcholine receptor antibody-positive disease undergoing planned surgery. No randomized trial or TAMG-specific active-comparator study has demonstrated that perioperative efgartigimod reduces postoperative myasthenic crisis or other surgical complications. Its optimal preoperative schedule and the value of routine postoperative continuation remain uncertain. Decisions about rapid immune optimization should consider the recent MG trajectory, bulbar and respiratory function, secretion clearance, operative demands, and available postoperative support. Surgical readiness requires multidisciplinary judgment tailored to the planned operation; it cannot be determined by a single clinical score, antibody level, or predetermined treatment course. The proposed dual-axis framework is intended to structure this discussion but has not been validated.

items.title: Long-term real-world outcomes of CD19-monitored rituximab retreatment in children with juvenile myasthenia gravis: A single-center retrospective cohort study.
items.journal: The Journal of international medical research
items.authors: Huiping Wang, Wenhao Duan, Zuohua Wang, Chunxia Wang, Qian Zhang, Wensha Nie
items.abstract: ObjectiveTo describe long-term outcomes after implementation of a CD19-monitored rituximab retreatment strategy in children with treatment-experienced juvenile myasthenia gravis.MethodsThis single-center retrospective cohort included patients initiating rituximab before age 18 between December 2016 and December 2024, followed through 28 February 2026. Induction comprised 1-2 intravenous doses of rituximab at 375 mg/m 2 . Retreatment was individualized using CD19+ B-cell reconstitution as a monitoring signal alongside clinical reassessment, without fixed maintenance dosing. Patients switching to efgartigimod were censored at the switching visit for rituximab efficacy analyses.ResultsTwenty-three of 28 screened patients were included. Ocular juvenile myasthenia gravis predominated at baseline (17/23 patients); rituximab was initiated for clinically meaningful treatment escalation. Median rituximab efficacy follow-up was 43.7 months, and patients received a median of four infusions. Median Myasthenia Gravis Activities of Daily Living score decreased from 6 to 0 at the last rituximab-related assessment. Eighteen patients achieved minimal manifestations or better, including 14 with complete stable remission. Prednisone was discontinued in 19/21 baseline users, and all 12 baseline nonsteroidal immunosuppressant users discontinued these agents. All 23 patients met a post hoc early-improvement criterion within 4 weeks; however, concomitant treatment and natural disease fluctuation limited attribution of this improvement to rituximab alone. Two patients (2/23; 8.7%) developed persistent hypogammaglobulinemia with documented intravenous immunoglobulin support and accounted for 14/17 postrituximab respiratory infection episodes. These patients had five infection-related hospital admissions; intravenous immunoglobulin was administered during four admissions.ConclusionsSustained clinical control and medication sparing were observed during follow-up after implementation of a CD19-monitored rituximab retreatment strategy in this predominantly ocular, uncontrolled cohort. This approach, incorporating clinical reassessment, may inform individualized pediatric rituximab management; prospective controlled studies are needed to establish treatment efficacy and validate retreatment thresholds. These findings, including infection-related hospital admissions, underscore the importance of longitudinal immunoglobulin and infection monitoring.

items.title: Real-world treatment patterns and disease burden in generalized myasthenia gravis patients receiving non-steroidal immunosuppressants within the Brazilian public health system: a claims database study.
items.authors: Acary Souza Bulle Oliveira, Marcondes Cavalcante França, Paulo Victor Sgobbi Souza, Ligia Coelho, Gabriela Kanevsky, Julio Cesar Barbour Oliveira
items.abstract: Generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) is a chronic autoimmune disorder affecting patients and healthcare systems. Limited real-world data exist on clinical journey and outcomes of patients with gMG within the Brazilian public health system (SUS). This study aimed to describe clinical profiles, treatment patterns, and healthcare resource use of patients with gMG receiving non-steroidal immunosuppressive therapy (NSIST) in SUS. This retrospective cohort study used DATASUS database claims data (2013-2023). Adults with gMG who initiated NSIST were assessed. Primary outcomes were treatment patterns, including therapeutic sequences and dosage adjustments. Secondary outcomes included exacerbation rates, myasthenic crises, and healthcare resource utilization, stratified by treatment line and patients. The study included 1,207 patients on NSIST, of whom 17.65% had severe gMG. The cohort was predominantly female (66.5%) with early-onset disease (62.6%). Azathioprine was the most common first immunotherapy (90.1%). Patients on the second immunotherapy had double the number of exacerbations (25.62 vs. 13.54 per 100 person-years [PY]) and crises (2.31 vs. 0.74 per 100 PY) than those on the first NSIST. Hospitalization and ICU admission rates also increased significantly. NSIST-treated severe gMG patients showed the highest observed clinical burden. Among NSIST-treated patients with gMG in the SUS, the disease imposed a substantial burden on both patients and the healthcare system, especially those requiring treatment escalation. These real-world findings offer descriptive evidence on the treatment patterns, clinical events, and healthcare resource use of NSIST-treated patients with gMG in the SUS and help identify the subgroups with the highest observed clinical and healthcare burden within this population.

items.title: Meningococcal ACWY quadrivalent conjugate vaccination responses in myasthenia gravis before complement inhibition.
items.authors: Sofia Marini, George Gyamfi-Brobbey, Jacopo Morroni, Silvia Falso, Federico Habetswallner, Martina Marini
items.abstract: Patients receiving complement inhibitor therapy are at increased risk of life-threatening meningococcal disease. Although quadrivalent meningococcal ACWY (MenACWY) vaccination is required before therapy initiation, the degree of seroprotection achieved in immunosuppressed patients and the importance of a second dose are uncertain. We evaluated serological protection after MenACWY vaccination in patients with myasthenia gravis (MG) undergoing complement inhibition. In this prospective cohort study, consecutive adults with MG candidates for complement inhibitors received one MenACWY conjugate vaccine dose at least two weeks before treatment initiation; a second dose was recommended because of prior or ongoing immunosuppression. Serological protection against meningococcal serogroups A, C, W, and Y was assessed using serum bactericidal antibody assay with baby rabbit complement. Titers of 1:8 or greater were considered protective. Among 43 patients, median age at vaccination was 55 years (IQR, 45-66 years) and 27 (63%) were female. Complete protection was achieved in 15/38 patients (39.5%) after the first dose and 21/38 (55.3%) after the second dose. In 33 patients with paired data after two doses, complete protection increased from 12 (36.4%) to 19 patients (57.6%; p = 0.02). Prior rituximab exposure was associated with lower complete protection after the first dose (1/11 vs 14/27; p = 0.03) and second dose (2/11 vs 19/27; p = 0.005). In patients with MG undergoing complement inhibition, one MenACWY vaccine dose provided complete protection in only 39.5% of patients. A second dose improved protection, supporting a two-dose vaccination schedule. Responses remained poor after rituximab exposure, favoring vaccination before B-cell-depleting therapy whenever possible.

items.title: Clinical features, diagnosis and outcomes of camrelizumab-induced myocarditis.
items.authors: Xiaojie Hu, Yong Pan, Zhaoquan Wu, Wei Sun, Chunjiang Wang
items.abstract: Background This study aimed to perform a pooled analysis of published case reports and case series to summarize the clinical characteristics, treatment patterns, and outcomes of camrelizumab-induced myocarditis. Methods Clinical reports of camrelizumab-induced myocarditis published up to May 31, 2026 were collected by searching Chinese and English databases; clinical data were then extracted and retrospectively analyzed. Results A total of 21 male (63.6%) and 12 female (36.4%) patients were enrolled, with a median age of 67 years (range: 44-77). The median time from camrelizumab initiation to myocarditis onset was 22.5 days (range: 1-180), and the median number of treatment cycles administered was 2 (range: 1-12). Patients were asymptomatic (18.2%) or experienced fatigue (36.4%), chest tightness (33.3%), shortness of breath (27.3%), palpitations (21.2%), and ptosis (21.2%). Laboratory tests revealed elevated cardiac injury biomarkers in affected patients. Electrocardiographic findings were variable, including normal tracings, ST-T segment changes (62.5%), sinus tachycardia (28.1%), premature ventricular contractions (18.8%), right bundle branch block (18.8%), and atrioventricular block (15.6%). Following camrelizumab discontinuation and treatment with systemic steroids plus intravenous immunoglobulin, 81.8% of patients achieved gradual symptomatic improvement. Ultimately, 12.1% of patients died of myocarditis-related complications. Conclusion Myocarditis is a fatal immune-related adverse event of camrelizumab. Cardiac injury biomarkers, clinical symptoms, and electrocardiographic changes should be routinely monitored during camrelizumab therapy. Individualized therapeutic regimens should be formulated according to disease severity, with systemic steroids and intravenous immunoglobulin as the first-line treatment.

items.title: Beyond Respiratory Failure: Unmasking Myasthenic Crisis in the Emergency Department.
items.authors: Rafeef Tahtamoni, Hamid Chatha
items.abstract: Myasthenic crisis is a life-threatening complication of myasthenia gravis (MG), typically presenting in patients with a known diagnosis. However, the absence of collateral history can delay recognition when respiratory failure is the initial manifestation. We report a 34-year-old male patient who presented to the emergency department with acute respiratory failure. Initial evaluation suggested airway compromise, but standard pulmonary, cardiac, and airway investigations were unrevealing. During hospitalization, he developed progressive bulbar and limb weakness, and a collateral history later revealed a prior diagnosis of MG treated with pyridostigmine. He required multiple intubations due to fluctuating muscle weakness and repeated extubation failures. The patient was treated with serial plasma exchange and corticosteroids, eventually stabilizing with a tracheostomy for prolonged ventilatory support. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of myasthenic crisis when collateral history is unavailable. Repeated extubation failures underscore the importance of careful assessment of bulbar and respiratory muscle function. Early, targeted interventions such as plasma exchange and corticosteroids are crucial to improving outcomes. Acute respiratory failure may be the initial presentation of myasthenic crisis. Prompt recognition, vigilant airway management, and early disease-specific therapy are essential for optimal patient outcomes.

items.title: Bulbar-Predominant Myasthenia Gravis Associated With Muscle-Specific Tyrosine Kinase Antibodies: A Diagnostic Challenge.
items.authors: Shirley Gandhi, Maleeha Abedi, Brianna Woodbeck, Sneh Parekh, Win Aung
items.abstract: Muscle-specific tyrosine kinase (MuSK) myasthenia gravis (MG) is an uncommon subtype of MG characterized by prominent bulbar and facial weakness with the potential for rapid progression and respiratory compromise. Patients are typically negative for acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibodies, which may contribute to delayed recognition and diagnosis. We present a 20-year-old postpartum woman who developed a sore throat followed by progressive dysphagia shortly after an uncomplicated vaginal delivery. Persistent and worsening bulbar symptoms prompted further neuromuscular evaluation. AChR antibodies were negative, whereas MuSK antibodies were markedly elevated at 1934 U/mL, supporting the diagnosis of MuSK-positive MG with predominant bulbar involvement. This case highlights the importance of considering MuSK-MG in patients with unexplained progressive bulbar symptoms despite negative AChR antibody testing. Early recognition of this clinical phenotype and appropriate serologic testing are essential to facilitate timely diagnosis and treatment.

items.title: Factors Influencing Publication Impact in Clinical Neuromuscular Disorders: A Bibliometric Analysis.
items.authors: Hebah F Qashqari, Anas S Alyazidi, Rawan O Daghistani, Osama Y Muthaffar, Ahmed K Bamaga, Mohammad A Almuhaizea
items.abstract: Bibliometric analysis provides an objective method to evaluate trends and patterns. Clinical neuromuscular medicine has evolved rapidly with advances in diagnostics, targeted therapies, and multidisciplinary care. Identifying the most influential research helps assess scientific impact and guide future directions. We performed a bibliometric analysis of the 50 most-cited articles in clinical neuromuscular using the Web of Science Core Collection. We evaluated citation metrics, study design, subspecialties, journal impact factor, funding source, and international collaborations. Data were retrieved through structured search strategies using Boolean operators. Analyses included performance metrics, network mapping, and regression and correlation testing. The literature demonstrates a marked shift toward high-impact therapeutic research. Citation velocity correlated strongly with publication year (r = 0.52, p < 0.001). Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), myasthenia gravis, and Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) were the leading topics. Clinical guidelines and consensus statements ranked among the most cited works, with SMA publications achieving the highest citation density (79.5 citations/year), highlighting the transformative effect of disease-modifying therapies. International collaboration significantly predicted impact, with multi-country studies achieving 65% higher citation rates. Industry-funded trials comprised 20% of top-cited articles and demonstrated high citation density. High-impact neurology and general medicine journals published most articles, though journal impact factor showed minimal correlation with citation performance. Disease-modifying therapies are reshaping neuromuscular care. Sustained international collaboration, patient-centered outcomes, and rigorous trial design remain essential to maximize global clinical impact.

items.title: Neurological adverse events associated with immune checkpoint inhibitors: a pharmacovigilance study based on the FAERS and JADER databases.
items.authors: Linghui Pan, Liu Ye
items.abstract: Neurological adverse events (NAEs) have been reported during immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy, but their reporting spectrum and onset patterns across drugs and pharmacovigilance databases remain incompletely characterized. We conducted a pharmacovigilance study of seven ICIs using the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) and the Japanese Adverse Drug Event Report (JADER) database. Primary drug-preferred term (PT) signals were evaluated using whole-database disproportionality analyses. An exploratory FAERS analysis compared PD-L1 with PD-1 inhibitors within study-defined tumor-indicator strata. Factors associated with NAE reporting were assessed in FAERS by univariate and multivariable logistic regression, and time-to-onset (TTO) was summarized using descriptive statistics and Weibull analyses. JADER cemiplimab data were summarized descriptively only because of sparse reporting. The analysis included 3,915 NAE reports from FAERS and 2,929 from JADER. The heatmaps displayed 111 positive drug-PT pairs across 31 PTs in FAERS and 49 across 16 PTs in JADER. Myasthenia gravis showed a disproportionality signal for all seven ICIs in non-Japanese FAERS reports and for all six ICIs included in the JADER signal analysis; encephalitis-related terms and immune-mediated myositis also recurred, although drug-specific patterns varied. In FAERS, complete-case regression included 111,879 ICI-related reports with 2,887 NAEs. Age ≥65 years and ICI combination therapy were associated with higher adjusted odds of NAE reporting, whereas PD-L1 and CTLA-4 monotherapy were associated with lower adjusted reporting odds relative to PD-1 monotherapy. The stratified comparison showed lower myasthenia gravis reporting odds for PD-L1 than PD-1 in both strata; encephalitis confidence intervals included 1. Drug-level median TTOs ranged from 16 to 43 days in FAERS and from 16 to 32 days in JADER, with heterogeneous Weibull patterns across drugs and databases. ICI-associated neurological reports showed recurring neuromuscular and central nervous system signals, partial qualitative concordance between non-Japanese FAERS reports and JADER, and heterogeneous onset patterns across drugs. The observed reporting associations do not establish comparative clinical safety. Overall, these findings are descriptive and hypothesis-generating and warrant confirmation in studies with exposure denominators, clinically adjudicated diagnoses, and longitudinal follow-up.

items.title: Autoimmune Overlap of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus and Myasthenia Gravis: A Case Report and Emerging Therapeutic Strategies.
items.authors: Bhavya Chadalavada, Ritesh Reddy Baddam, Isabelle Sinitsa, Rohan K Dhamsania
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and myasthenia gravis (MG) are autoimmune disorders that predominantly affect women and may coexist, though their overlap remains rare. Shared mechanisms, including loss of immune tolerance, B-cell hyperactivity, and dysregulated cytokine signaling, are thought to underlie this association. We report the case of a 56-year-old woman diagnosed with seronegative MG after presenting with progressive proximal weakness, ocular involvement, and electrophysiologic evidence of neuromuscular junction dysfunction. She was stabilized on IVIG, pyridostigmine, and azathioprine. Four years later, she developed a malar rash, polyarthralgia, and bilateral upper-extremity numbness; serologic evaluation confirmed SLE and revealed newly detectable acetylcholine receptor binding antibodies, representing her first positive MG serologic marker. Hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) and methotrexate were added to her regimen. Efgartigimod alfa, a neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) antagonist, was subsequently initiated for persistent MG and produced marked improvement in MG Activities of Daily Living (MG-ADL) scores. Her SLE-related joint symptoms also improved, although SLE-directed therapy had been adjusted during the same period. However, cyclic dosing resulted in consistent symptomatic wear-off in the days preceding each treatment cycle. Transition to nipocalimab, a fixed-schedule anti-FcRn monoclonal antibody providing continuous IgG suppression, is under multidisciplinary consideration. This case highlights the diagnostic and therapeutic complexity of SLE-MG overlap and suggests that FcRn inhibition may offer a mechanistically rational approach to IgG-mediated disease in both conditions, a possibility that warrants further study.

items.title: Good's syndrome and infections in a large retrospective cohort of thymoma.
items.authors: Wenji Jia, Lei Jin, Xiao Huan, Chong Yan, Jianying Xi, Liewen Pang, Chongbo Zhao, Jie Song, Xianglin Chu, Sushan Luo
items.abstract: Good's syndrome (GS) is an immunodeficiency associated with thymoma characterized by hypogammaglobulinemia. The co-existence of recurrent infections may be associated with quality of life and overall survival. Despite its relevance, the impact of GS on patients with thymoma has rarely been studied in large cohorts. This is a retrospective cohort study of patients with pathologically confirmed thymoma recruited between May 2010 and November 2024. Data on peripheral immune profile, infections, and paraneoplastic syndrome (PNS) were collected and analyzed. Of 1001 patients with thymoma, we ultimately included 158 patients who underwent peripheral immune profiling. The prevalence of GS was 45.6% (72/158), and the infections were reported in 43.69% (69/158). Infection rates were higher in the GS group than in non-GS group (50% versus 32.72%, P = 0.0384). Among the 121 pathogens identified from this cohort, bacteria were the most prevalent (52.07%, 63/121), followed by fungi (34.71%, 42/121) and virus (13.22%, 16/121). Patients with infections had significantly lower overall survival compared with those without infections (P < 0.001). In addition, patients with multiple PNS had poorer survival than those with a single PNS (P < 0.001). No significant difference in overall survival was found between the GS and the non-GS groups. GS and infections are prevalent in patients with thymoma. Infections and multiple PNS were associated with poorer survival outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of early detection and intervention for improving prognosis and long-term survival in patients with thymoma.
